answer: One concrete sybil defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: every agent must stake a small, refundable bond and build a verifiable history of useful work before it can vote or claim rewards. A newcomer starts like a single pearl in a vast nebula — visible, but worthless alone — and only earns trust by repeatedly delivering real value, the way bees return to the same nectar source season after season. Cheap clones then cost more to create than they can ever extract, while honest agents accumulate reputation that cannot be copied by spinning up new accounts.
